'''Delon Reginald Wright<ref>{{cite web|title=Delon Wright's Fashion Guide on Cabbie Presents|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Sp5z94Ov-48|work=TSN|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=October 13, 2018}}</ref><ref name=BirthIndex>{{cite web|title=Delon Reginald Wright|url=https://www.californiabirthindex.org/birth/delon_reginald_wright_born_1992_21902017|publisher=CaliforniaBirthIndex|access-date=December 29, 2019}}</ref>''' (born April 26, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[New York Knicks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[City College of San Francisco|CC of San Francisco Rams]] and the [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah Utes]], being a first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] player in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]] in 2014 and 2015. He also earned the [[Bob Cousy Award]] in 2015.

==High school and junior college==
[[File:DelonWright Utes.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Wright in 2015 at Utah.]]
Born in [[Los Angeles, California]],<ref>{{cite web | title = Wright CBSSports.com profile | work = [[CBSSports.com]] | url = http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/players/playerpage/2105158/delon-wright | access-date = December 22, 2014}}</ref> Wright led [[Leuzinger High School]] to the California state championship as a senior and was named [[CIF Southern Section]] Division 1A Player of the Year.  Despite his athletic high school success, he struggled academically and failed to graduate, which led him to enroll at [[California Community College Athletic Association]] (CCCAA) school the [[City College of San Francisco]], because California State law allowed him to attend without having finished high school yet.<ref>{{cite web | last = Auerbach| first = Nicole| title = Utah's Delon Wright is unheralded and nearly unmatched | work = [[USA Today]] | date =  March 10, 2015| url = https://usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/pac12/2015/03/10/delon-wright-utah-utes-basketball-nba/24715789/ | access-date = December 19, 2024}}</ref> After two successful seasons there, he committed to Utah over [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]], [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]], [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] and [[Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball|Saint Mary's]], despite the Utes winning only 6 games the previous season, where he majored in sociology.<ref>{{cite web | last = Johnson| first = Raphielle| title = 6–5 City College of San Francisco point guard Delon Wright commits to Utah | work = [[NBCSports.com]] | date =  September 21, 2012| url = https://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2012/09/21/6-5-city-college-of-san-francisco-point-guard-delon-wright-commits-to-utah/ | access-date = December 22, 2014}}</ref>

==College career==
In his first season at Utah, Wright immediately became one of the top players in the [[Pac-12 Conference]].<ref>{{cite web| last = Hill| first = Bonta| title = Fomer [sic] CCSF standout Delon Wright makes seamless transition to Division I at Utah| work = [[San Francisco Examiner]]| date = March 4, 2014| url = http://www.sfexaminer.com/sanfrancisco/fomer-ccsf-standout-delon-wright-makes-seamless-transition-to-division-i-at-utah/Content?oid=2720323| access-date = December 22, 2014| archive-date = December 22, 2014| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141222153804/http://www.sfexaminer.com/sanfrancisco/fomer-ccsf-standout-delon-wright-makes-seamless-transition-to-division-i-at-utah/Content?oid=2720323| url-status = dead}}</ref> He finished in the top 10 in the conference in [[Points per game|scoring]] (seventh at 16.9 points per game), [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] (third at 4.89), [[Steal (basketball)|steals]] (first at 2.56), [[blocked shot]]s (sixth at 1.3), [[field goal percentage]] (third at 56.1 percent) and [[free throw percentage]] (ninth at 80.5 percent).  Wright additionally averaged 6.8 [[rebounds per game]], despite playing the [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] position.<ref>{{cite web| title =Delon Wright Utah Utes bio| work =[[Utah Utes]]| url =http://www.utahutes.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/delon_wright_845505.html| access-date =December 22, 2014| url-status =dead| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20141227174028/http://www.utahutes.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/delon_wright_845505.html| archive-date =December 27, 2014}}</ref> At the conclusion of the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14 season]], Wright became the first Ute to be named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] and was also named to the league's All-Defensive team.<ref>{{cite web | last = Facer| first = Dick| title = Utah basketball: Delon Wright makes Pac-12 history for Runnin' Utes | work = [[Deseret News]] | date = March 10, 2014 | url = http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865598328/Utes-Delon-Wright-named-to-All-Pac-12-first-team.html?pg=all | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140311161313/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865598328/Utes-Delon-Wright-named-to-All-Pac-12-first-team.html?pg=all | url-status = dead | archive-date = March 11, 2014 | access-date = December 22, 2014}}</ref> Following the season, Wright considered entering the [[2014 NBA draft]], but ultimately decided to return to Utah for his senior season.<ref name=DRAFT/>

At the start of his senior season, Wright was named to the 50-man watch lists for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]]<ref>{{cite web | last = Judd| first = Brandon| title = BYU's Haws, Utah's Wright named to Naismith Trophy watch list | work = [[Deseret News]] | date = December 3, 2014 | url = http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865616896/BYUs-Haws-Utahs-Wright-named-to-Naismith-Trophy-watch-list.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141212192836/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865616896/BYUs-Haws-Utahs-Wright-named-to-Naismith-Trophy-watch-list.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = December 12, 2014 | access-date = December 22, 2014}}</ref> and the [[John R. Wooden Award]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Utah's Delon Wright Named to Wooden Award Watch List | work = [[Utah Utes]] | date = November 17, 2014 | url = http://www.utahutes.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111714aaa.html | access-date = December 22, 2014 | archive-date = December 27, 2014 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141227174209/http://www.utahutes.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111714aaa.html | url-status = dead }}</ref> For the second-straight season, he was voted first-team All-Pac-12 and again named to the Pac-12 All-Defensive Team.<ref>{{cite press release |title=2014–15 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors |date=March 9, 2015 |publisher=Pac-12 |url=https://pac-12.com/news/2015/3/9/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150312012307/http://pac-12.com/article/2015/03/09/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors |archive-date=March 12, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> Wright was also a two-time member of the Pac-12 All-Defensive team and won the 2015 [[Bob Cousy Award]].

Wright became the first player in Utah men's basketball history to be named to the first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] in consecutive years ([[2013–14 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|2014]] and [[2014–15 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|2015]]).

==Professional career==
===Toronto Raptors (2015–2019)===
On June 25, 2015, Wright was selected with the 20th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/wright-powell-062515|title=Raptors Tab Wright With 20th Pick, Acquire Future First-Round Pick & Rights To Norman Powell From Bucks|date=June 25, 2015|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=June 26, 2015}}</ref> On July 3, 2015, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Raptors and joined the team for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/delonwright-070315|title=Raptors Sign First-Round Pick Delon Wright|date=July 3, 2015|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=July 3, 2015}}</ref> On April 8, 2016, with All-Stars [[DeMar DeRozan]] and [[Kyle Lowry]] rested, Wright scored a season-high 19 points in a 111–98 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160408/INDTOR/gameinfo.html|title=Raptors keep Pacers waiting for playoffs with 111–98 win|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=April 8, 2016|access-date=April 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170321202014/http://www.nba.com/games/20160408/INDTOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 21, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments with [[Raptors 905]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref name=assignments>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=January 3, 2018}}</ref>

Wright missed much of the 2016–17 season with a right shoulder injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/delon-wright-injury-update/080116|title=Delon Wright Injury Update|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=August 1, 2016|access-date=August 2, 2016}}</ref> He also had multiple assignments to Raptors 905.<ref name="assignments" />

On January 3, 2018, Wright set career highs with 25 points and 13 rebounds in a 124–115 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]]. He had his first career double-double and hit four 3-pointers to lead the second unit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975306|title=DeRozan scores 35 points, Raptors beat Bulls 124–115|publisher=ESPN|date=January 3, 2018|access-date=January 3, 2018}}</ref>

Before the trade to the Grizzlies he averaged nearly 7 points per game during his last season with the Raptors.

===Memphis Grizzlies (2019)===
On February 7, 2019, Wright, [[C. J. Miles]], [[Jonas Valančiūnas]] and a 2024 second-round draft pick were traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[Marc Gasol]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-release/raptors-acquire-gasol-from-grizzlies|title=Raptors Acquire Gasol From Grizzlies|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 7, 2019|access-date=February 7, 2019}}</ref> On April 5, he scored a career-high 26 points in a 122–112 victory over the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. He also recorded his first career triple-double adding 14 assists and 10 rebounds. Two days later, on April 7, Wright posted his second triple-double with 20 points, 12 assists and 13 rebounds in a 129–127 victory over the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. On April 10, Wright posted his third triple-double with 13 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists in a 132–117 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]]. He averaged 12.2 ppg with the Grizzlies.

===Dallas Mavericks (2019–2020)===
On July 8, 2019, Wright was acquired by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in a [[sign-and-trade deal]] with the Memphis Grizzlies in exchange for two-second-round picks and the draft rights to [[Satnam Singh]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-make-it-official-acquiring-veteran-guard-delon-wright/|title=Mavericks make it official, acquiring veteran guard Delon Wright|publisher=mavs.com|date=July 8, 2019|access-date=July 8, 2019}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons (2020–2021)===
On November 27, 2020, Wright was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], who received [[Trevor Ariza]] from Detroit and two second round picks from Dallas.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-delon-wright-dallas-three-team-trade|title=Detroit Pistons Acquire Delon Wright From Dallas In Three-Team Trade|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=November 27, 2020|access-date=November 27, 2020}}</ref> On January 25, 2021, Wright set a career high with 28 points in a 119–104 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401267417|title = 76ers vs. Pistons – Game Recap – January 25, 2021 – ESPN}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2021)===
On March 25, 2021, Wright was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for [[Cory Joseph]] and two future second-round draft picks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Acquire Delon Wright|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-delon-wright|website=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2021|access-date=March 26, 2021}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2021–2022)===
On August 7, 2021, Wright was traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in a three-team trade with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Delon Wright|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-delon-wright|website=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2021|access-date=August 7, 2021}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2022–2024)===
On July 6, 2022, Wright signed a two-year, $16 million contract with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards Sign Delon Wright|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-delon-wright|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2022|access-date=July 6, 2022}}</ref> On March 24, 2023, Wright scored a season-high 24 points and grabbed seven rebounds during a 136–124 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Quillen | first=Ian Nicholas | title=Kispert's 3s help Wizards pull away from Spurs 136-124 | website=AP News | date=2023-03-25 | url=https://apnews.com/article/spurs-wizards-corey-kispert-deni-avdija-d01fcb263168f4f3229b8debd57b5f2c | access-date=2025-05-29}}</ref>
On February 16, 2024, he was waived by the Wizards.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards Request Waivers on Wright|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-request-waivers-on-wright|website=NBA.com|date=February 16, 2024|access-date=February 17, 2024}}</ref>

===Miami Heat (2024)===
On February 18, 2024, Wright signed with the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN DELON WRIGHT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-delon-wright|website=NBA.com|date=February 18, 2024|access-date=February 18, 2024}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2024–2025)===
On July 7, 2024, Wright signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Delon Wright|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-delon-wright|website=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2024|access-date=July 15, 2024}}</ref> On December 17, 2024, Wright and the Bucks won the [[2024 NBA Cup]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Kirschenbaum | first=Alex | title=Bucks Beat Thunder to Win First NBA Cup, Giannis Antetokounmpo Named MVP | website=Milwaukee Bucks On SI | date=2024-12-18 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/bucks/onsi/news/bucks-beat-thunder-to-win-first-nba-cup-giannis-antetokounmpo-named-mvp-ak1987 | access-date=2025-12-10}}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2025)===
On February 6, 2025, Wright was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in a multi-team trade.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks-acquire-delon-wright-and-hugo-besson|title=Knicks Acquire Delon Wright and Hugo Besson|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025}}</ref> In 14 appearances (five starts) for New York, Wright averaged 4.3 points, 1.4 rebounds, and 2.1 assists.

On September 27, 2025, Wright signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|title= Indiana Pacers Transactions - Sept. 27, 2025 | Indiana Pacers|url= https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-transactions-sept-27-2025 |work= nba.com|date=September 27, 2025}}</ref> On October 9, the Pacers waived Wright.<ref>{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Transactions - Oct. 9, 2025|url= https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-transactions-oct-9-2025|work= nba.com|date=October 9, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
